# Engineering Standards — Distribution Index

- **Version**: `v0.1.1`
- **Released**: 2026-05-20
- **Changelog**: [CHANGELOG.md](./CHANGELOG.md)

This directory is the **compiled output** of the Engineering Standards corpus authored under `source/`. Consumer repositories pull a stack's subtree via the `@org/standards-sync` CLI; see the consumer-side documentation for the sync flow.

Compiled artifacts are regenerated **only** by the release workflow under the `@engineering-standards-bot` GitHub App identity. Human-authored edits to any file inside this directory are rejected by the `dist-protection-lint` PR status check; see ADR-0004 for the four-guard protection model.

## Layout

Each `stacks/<stack-id>/` subdirectory follows the canonical layout:

```text
stacks/<stack-id>/
├── cursor/
│   └── rules/                 # Cursor MDC files — one .mdc per applicable rule.
├── copilot/
│   └── copilot-instructions.md # Concatenated rules for GitHub Copilot.
├── claude/
│   └── CLAUDE.md              # Concatenated rules for Claude Skills.
├── junie/
│   └── AGENTS.md              # Numbered-list format for JetBrains Junie.
├── agents-md/
│   └── AGENTS.md              # Universal AGENTS.md (≤150 lines).
└── memory-bank/               # Six-file Memory Bank scaffold.
```

## How to consume

Run the consumer sync CLI from the root of your project:

```bash
npx @org/standards-sync
```

The CLI detects your stack from `pom.xml` / `package.json` / `pyproject.toml`, resolves the pinned version from `.standards-version` (or the latest release tag), and copies the matching `stacks/<stack-id>/` subtree into your project's conventional locations. See the `@org/standards-sync` README for details.

## Releases

Tag history:

```bash
git tag --list 'v*' --sort=-version:refname
```

Audit the bot-authored release commits:

```bash
git log --author='engineering-standards-bot' --pretty='%h %ai %s' -- dist/
```
